correlates.name: Pulmonary nocardiosis
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old kidney transplant recipient on tacrolimus and prednisone who gardens daily. Three weeks of fever, productive cough and a 4-kg weight loss, then 2 days of headache and new left arm weakness. T 38.4 C, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94%; crackles at the right apex.
correlates.workup: Chest CT: several nodules, some cavitating; brain MRI: a ring-enhancing lesion. Sputum: gram-positive branching filaments that are weakly acid-fast with a mild decolorizer; aerobic and catalase-positive.
correlates.management: A sulfonamide (TMP-SMX); image the brain, since spread there (and to skin) is common.

correlates.name: Actinomycosis
correlates.presentation: 46-year-old man with many decayed teeth who had a lower molar pulled 6 weeks ago. A firm, slowly enlarging swelling at the angle of the jaw now drains pus through the skin; 3 weeks of low fever and cough. T 37.9 C; hard, painless jaw mass with a draining tract.
correlates.workup: Pus contains hard yellow grains made of tangled gram-positive branching filaments; not acid-fast; grows only anaerobically and is catalase-negative. Chest film: right lower lobe infiltrate.
correlates.management: Penicillin; fix the dental disease, since the organism is normal mouth flora that reaches the lung when aspirated.

correlates.name: Cholera
correlates.presentation: Relief worker, 34, in a post-earthquake camp drinking river water. Since yesterday: sudden painless, profuse watery diarrhea, pale gray with mucus flecks, a liter an hour; vomiting, leg cramps; no fever or blood. T 36.9 C, HR 128, BP 78/44; sunken eyes, skin tenting.
correlates.workup: Stool: no white cells or blood; culture on thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose agar grows yellow colonies. K+ 2.8 mEq/L, HCO3- 14 mEq/L, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Replace fluid and electrolytes fast (oral rehydration solution, IV if in shock): with it, deaths fall from 25-50% to few. Reportable to the CDC.

correlates.name: Measles
correlates.presentation: Unvaccinated 4-year-old, 10 days after a crowded indoor party: 3 days of fever to 40.5 C, cough, runny nose, red watery eyes, light sensitivity, then a dense red rash spreading from the face to trunk and limbs. Small red spots with bluish-white centers inside the cheeks.
correlates.management: Supportive: acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever, possibly vitamin A; nothing lowers the viral load. Airborne isolation (negative pressure, N95), since the virus lingers up to 2 hours; it is reportable.

correlates.name: Dengue
correlates.presentation: 27-year-old back 5 days from a month in Thailand, many mosquito bites. Sudden high fever, chills, severe headache, pain behind the eyes and intense pain in the back, joints, muscles and bones; a red blotchy rash on the trunk. T 39.8 C, HR 104, BP 118/72.
correlates.management: Supportive only: there is no antiviral and no vaccine. Watch for leaky vessels and shock, mainly with a second infection by another serotype (15% mortality untreated, about 1% with supportive care).
